issues.display_title: Issue #24: Fix Issue Photographers Statistic Counter Displays 0
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A bug was found on the hero section of the main page at https://360photographers.org/.

The global statistics component displays "0 PHOTOGRAPHERS". This is highly contradictory because:

  1. The map below it (Live Coverage) shows many photographer pins located all over the world.
  2. The Search the Directory form indicates available data (e.g., displaying "20 results").
  3. The small kicker text above the main heading also shows "0 VERIFIED PHOTOGRAPHERS".

This issue is likely caused by one of:

  • The Frontend failing to properly bind the data from the API response to the UI component.
  • A variable being hardcoded to 0.
  • The Backend global stats API failing to execute the count query properly and returning 0/null.

Subtasks

  1. Audit State Binding: Inspect the UI components rendering the 0 PHOTOGRAPHERS and 0 VERIFIED PHOTOGRAPHERS text. Ensure these components are listening to and extracting the state from the correct API response.
  2. Loading State: Ensure that while data is still being fetched, the UI displays a skeleton loader or a loading indicator instead of instantly rendering a permanent fallback of 0.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The large number on the "PHOTOGRAPHERS" counter displays the actual, accurate total of all registered and searchable photographers in the directory.
  • The small navigation/kicker text "X VERIFIED PHOTOGRAPHERS" above the main title also displays the accurate total number.
  • The numbers automatically update when new photographers are added to the database.

Scenario Testing (for tester)

Pre-condition: open the home page https://360photographers.org/ and let it fully load.

#ScenarioStepsExpected result
1Main counter shows real total1. Open the home page.
2. Read the large "PHOTOGRAPHERS" number in the hero.		Shows the actual total (a non-zero, correct count) — not 0.
2Kicker text matches1. Read the small "X VERIFIED PHOTOGRAPHERS" text above the main heading.Shows the same accurate total as the main counter.
3Consistency with directory1. Note the counter value.
2. Compare against the Search the Directory results count and the number of map pins.		The counter is consistent with the available data (no longer contradicts the map/search).
4Loading state (no flash of 0)1. Hard-refresh the page (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R) and watch the hero while it loads.A skeleton/loading indicator is shown while fetching — the counter does not briefly or permanently show 0.
5Slow network1. In DevTools, throttle network to "Slow 3G".
2. Reload the page.		Loader shows during fetch; once data arrives the real number appears. No permanent 0.
6Auto-update on new data1. Add a new photographer to the directory (or use a staging dataset).
2. Reload the home page.		The counter total increases to reflect the new photographer.
7API failure handling1. Simulate the global-stats API failing (block/return error in DevTools).
2. Reload.		The UI degrades gracefully (loader / retry / hidden) rather than presenting a misleading 0 as a real value.
8Cross-device / browser1. Repeat scenarios 1–2 on mobile viewport and on Chrome + Safari/Firefox.Accurate counts display consistently across devices and browsers.

Source: bug report on the 360photographers.org hero global-statistics counter.

RESULT

Root cause: getPhotographerCount.go sub-location query used wrong column name latitude instead of actual DB column latilatitude (intentional typo in photographer_sublocations table, also referenced in directory_photographer_sublocation.go model and getBulkCityPhotographerCounts.go). Mismatched column caused the agency-photographer sub-total query to fail/return 0, dragging the global count to 0.

Fixed in commit 9969e03 (already on main): both occurrences of photographer_sublocations.latitude / ps.latitude corrected to latilatitude in src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerCount.go. Verified consistent with existing usage elsewhere in codebase. No further code changes needed.

issues.display_title: Issue #25: Fix Issue Location Data Displays Empty Punctuation Characters ( ,' ) on Photographer Detail Page
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A data binding or API response bug was found on the Photographer Detail page. There is an inconsistency in how location data is rendered between the directory card component on the home page and the detailed profile page.

Issue Details:

  1. On the Home/Directory Page (Works): In the photographer list card, the location is successfully fetched and rendered correctly, for example: TORONTO, CANADA.
  2. On the Photographer Detail Page (Broken): When navigating to a specific profile (URL: https://360photographers.org/photographer/alin-bugeag-iki6), the "LOCATION" section fails to render the city and country names. The UI only displays a comma and a single quote/apostrophe: ,'.

This indicates that the UI template might be hardcoding the punctuation (e.g. {{city}}, {{country}}'), but the data variables are coming up empty (null or undefined) specifically on this detail page endpoint.

Sub-tasks

  1. Audit State Binding: Inspect the UI component for the Location section on the Photographer Detail page. Ensure the variables bound for the city and country match exactly with the ones used in the Home page card component.
  2. Conditional Rendering: Fix the template string formatting. If the city or country data is unavailable (null), do not render the comma (,) or apostrophe so the UI remains clean.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The Photographer Detail page displays the full location name (e.g. "Toronto, Canada"), exactly as it appears on the Home page card.
  • No leftover punctuation characters (like ,') are displayed if the location data is genuinely empty in the database.

RESULT

Root cause: getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go (used by Photographer Detail page) did not include city, country, continent fields in its location object — unlike the directory listing endpoint (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go locationMap), causing the frontend template to render empty ,'.

Fixed in commit 9969e03 (already on main): location object now includes city, country, continent (derived from Preload(\"City.Country.Continent\"), nil-safe), matching the structure/keys used by the directory listing endpoint. No further code changes needed.
